description:
FOUND s473t5e (#1501 round 6, `re/` CHECK 2) as t/re/subst_amp.t's ONE fact --
all 13 of its blessed rows, the file's whole plan -- and, while probing it, as
a HANG in ordinary Perl code.

perl's rule for a global match (pp_hot.c's `REXEC_NOT_FIRST` / `gofs`): when a
match is ZERO-LENGTH, the next attempt is made AT THE SAME POSITION with a
zero-length match PROHIBITED, and only if that fails does the position bump
along.  PCL has neither half consistently.

PROBED (scratch/s473t5e/probe-zerowidth2.pl), perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl:

                                          perl                    PCL
  $_='xxxx'; s/\d*|x/<$&>/g            <><x><><x><><x><><x><>  <>x<>x<>x<>x<>
  ('xax' =~ /\d*|x/g) in LIST          6 matches [|x|||x|]     4  [|||]
  $p='abc'; $p=~/b*/g three times      pos 0, 2, 2             pos 0, 0, 0
  s/x*/-/g on 'abc'                    -a-b-c-                 -a-b-c-   (same)
  s/X*/./g on 'aXbXc'                  .a..b..c.               .a..b..c. (same)
  split /x*/, 'abc'                    a,b,c                   a,b,c     (same)
  () = ('aaa' =~ /a*/g)                2                       2         (same)

TWO HALVES, and the first is the serious one:

(a) THE SCALAR `//g` ITERATOR NEVER ADVANCES past a zero-length match, so it
    never terminates.  `pos` stays where it was, measured above (0, 0, 0).
    `while ($s =~ /\d*|x/g) { ... }` runs for ever; with anything accumulating
    in the loop it dies of HEAP EXHAUSTION, which is what
    scratch/s473t5e/probe-zerowidth.pl does (SBCL prints the whole heap table
    and quits after ~700 MB of `[]@0`).  `while (/(\w*)/g)` is an ordinary
    Perl idiom, so this is not a test-suite curiosity.

(b) `s///g` AND LIST `//g` BUMP instead of retrying.  Where the pattern can
    match both empty and non-empty at one position (`\d*|x`), perl takes the
    empty match, then retries at the same position with empty forbidden and
    takes `x`; PCL takes the empty match and moves on, so every non-empty
    alternative at that position is lost.

    Note WHY the pure-empty cases agree: `s/x*/-/g` on 'abc' needs only the
    bump, not the retry, so PCL's bump-always loop gives perl's answer.  The
    divergence needs an ALTERNATION (or any pattern that can match both ways
    at one position), which is why this went unnoticed.

ROWS: t/re/subst_amp.t 13 (its whole plan -- the file is subst.t's `$&`-enabled
twin and its first assertion is exactly `s/\d*|x/<$&>/g`), plus part of
t/re/subst.t's 67.  The infinite loop (a) is also a candidate explanation for
suite files that TIMEOUT with no output; it was not searched for this round.

FIX SHAPE: ONE reading, in whatever the global-match loop is
(`p-subst`'s `g` path and the `p-=~` scalar `//g` iterator must both ask it --
they are two copies today, which is how they came to differ: (a) does not bump
and (b) does not retry, in the same codebase).  The rule is a single boolean
carried across the attempt: "the last match at this position was zero-length,
so this attempt must be non-empty"; on failure, advance one CHARACTER (not one
code unit -- mind the surrogate pair question if it ever matters) and clear it.

ACCEPTANCE BAR: the seven-row probe above identical to perl; t/re/subst_amp.t
0/13 -> 13/0; `while ($s =~ /(\w*)/g)` terminates; and the four cases that
ALREADY agree stay agreeing (they are the regression risk -- a retry added
without the bump turns `s/x*/-/g` into its own infinite loop).  A `cl/` change,
so the FULL sweep plus the re/ + op/ companion legs.

=== DONE (s484c) ===
SHIPPED 2026-09-14, commit "s484c member 1 (#1719): perl's global-match advance
rule, ONE reading" (runtime-only; no generation bump).

perl's rule is a MINEND, not "advance one character": after a zero-length match
the next attempt is made AT THE SAME POSITION with the empty match forbidden --
which lets a longer alternative there win -- and only its failure moves on.
The constraint is a zero-width :filter appended to the pattern in a parse tree
(%pcl-build-minend-scanner, memoized by the existing scanner cache, built only
when a plain scan actually returns an empty match at the position).  ONE
reading, %p-global-scan; five loops ask it -- the scalar iterator, list //g,
the \G-anchored list, s///g and split.  The iterator's state is pos() PLUS the
zero-length flag (perl's MGf_MINMATCH) in one value, so p-pos now normalises an
out-of-range assignment the way magic_setpos does (pos()=-2 used to store -2
and crash the next match inside cl-ppcre).  s///g also stops re-scanning the
subject just to count.

MEASURED: the task's 7-row table, 9 termination/\G rows, 23 split spellings, a
19-row global-match battery and 6 pos() edge cases all identical to perl
5.40.3.  t/re/subst_amp.t 0/13 -> 1/12 and t/re/subst.t 205/67 -> 206/66, both
spliced with this cause.  The task's PREDICTION of subst_amp.t 0/13 -> 13/0 was
WRONG: exactly one of its rows is this task's (line 14), the other twelve are
(?{ CODE }) regex code blocks.  Bench (startup subtracted, min of 6, shared
box): the m//g scanning loop -0.9 %, -2.4 %, -4.6 % (order reversed) -- no
cost; the s///g loop -8.9 %.  Guard Pl/t/global-match-01.t (4 rows, each child
under a timeout so a regression FAILS instead of hanging), inverse-verified.
ir-spec Â§10-gmatch is normative.  Residue filed as #1751 (after s///g perl's $1
is the LAST match's capture, PCL's the FIRST).
subject: a ZERO-LENGTH match does not advance `pos`, so `while ($s =~ /(\w*)/g)` NEVER TERMINATES (heap exhaustion), and `s/\d*|x/<$&>/g` takes the empty branch at every position where perl retries the SAME position non-emptily -- t/re/subst_amp.t's whole 13 rows
